la:verb:perpurgo.html:
per-purgo (ante-class. perpūrĭgo, v. Ritschl, Opusc. 2, 426 sqq.), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to cleanse or purge thoroughly, to make quite clean.
Lit.: alvum,: se,: perpurgata ulcera,, n. 36: perpurigatis auribus,i. e. with the greatest attention,.—
Trop., to clear up, explain: locus orationis perpurgatus ab iis, qui ante me dixerunt,: crimina,; cf. .—Absol.: de dote tanto magis perpurga,settle, arrange,.

la:adj:perpetuus.gloss: perpetual, everlasting, continuous, uninterrupted, constant, incessant, unbroken
senses: perpetual, everlasting, continuous, uninterrupted, constant, incessant, unbroken
ablative of time: a duration of time, an entirety, all throughout
la:adj:perpetuus.html:
per-pĕtŭus, a, um, adj. (
comp. perpetuior, Cato ap. P.; sup. perpetuissimus, ) [peto], continuing throughout, continuous, unbroken, uninterrupted; constant, universal, general, entire, whole, perpetual (syn.: continuus, assiduus): sulcos perpetuos ducere,: quin aedes totae perpetuae ruant,: agmen,: munitiones,: palus,: milites disposuit perpetuis vigiliisque stationibusque,: perpetuis soliti patres considere mensis,: vescitur Aeneas ... perpetui tergo bovis,: Apenninus perpetuis jugis ab Alpibus tendens ad Siculum fretum,: tractus,: oratio perpetua (opp. altercatio),; cf. : disputatio,; : quaestiones perpetuae hoc adulescente constitutae sunt,a standing commission, a permanent tribunal for criminal investigation,: perpetua historia, a continuous or general history, : colere te usque perpetuom diem,: diem perpetuum in laetitiā degere,this whole day,: triduum,: biennium,: ignis Vestae perpetuus ac sempiternus,: lex perpetua et aeterna,: stellarum perennes cursus atque perpetui,. stabilis et perpetua permansio, : voluntas mea perpetua et constans in rem publicam,: formido,: assidua et perpetua cura,: perpetui scrinia Sili,of the immortal Silius,.—As subst.: perpĕtŭum, i, n., the abiding, permanent (opp. temporale), .—Hence: in perpetuum (sc. tempus), for all time, forever, in perpetuity, constantly: mulier repperit odium ocius Suā inmunditiā, quam in perpetuom ut placeat munditia sua. : serva tibi in perpetuom amicum me,: in perpetuum comprimi,; : obtinere aliquid in perpetuum,: non in perpetuum irascetur, et saep.—So, in perpetuum modum = perpetuo, .—
In partic.
That holds constantly and universally, universal, general: perpetui juris et universi generis quaestio,: nec arbitror perpetuum quicquam in hoc praecipi posse,: ne id quidem perpetuum est,does not always hold good,: illud in quo quasi certamen est controversiae ... id ita dici placet, ut traducatur ad perpetuam quaestionem, to a general principle,

.—

In augury: perpetua fulmina, perpetual lighlnings, i. e. whose prognostics refer to one's whole life, .—
In gram.: perpetuus modus,the infinitive mood, P. —Hence, adv., in three forms, perpetuo (class.), perpetuum (poet.), and perpetue (late Lat.).
perpĕtŭō, constantly, uninterruptedly, perpetually, always, forever, utterly, hopelessly: perpetuon' valuisti?: metuo ne technae meae perpetuo perierint,: dico ut perpetuo pereas,; so, perpetuo perire,: opinionem retinere,: loquens,: sub imperio esse,; .—
perpĕtŭum, constantly, uninterruptedly, perpetually: uti,.—
perpĕtŭē, constantly, .

la:adj:perpaucus.html:
per-paucus, a, um, adj.,
very little, very few: homines,; cf. in tmesi: per pol quam paucos reperias amatores,: patres,: si perpauca mutavisset,: dicere,; cf.: perpauca loquens,: gens perpauca,.—Sup., .

la:verb:perpolio.html:
per-pŏlĭo, īvi, ītum (
fut. perpolibo, ), 4, v. a., to polish well.
Lit.: loco calce arenāque perpolito,: aurum tritu perpolitum,: caudae setas horridas comptā diligentiā perpolibo,; cf. .—
Trop., to polish, perfect, finish, put the finishing hand to (class.): opus,: perpolire et absolvere aliquid,: perpolire atque conficere,: perpoliendi labor,: ea, quae habes instituta, perpolies,.— Hence, perpŏlītus, a, um, P. a., thoroughly polished or refined: homines perfecti in dicendo et perpoliti,: qui non sit omnibus iis artibus perpolitus,; so, litteris perpolitus,: vita perpolita humanitate (opp. immanis),: oratio,: explicatio,.—Hence, adv.: perpŏlītē, in a very polished manner; in sup.: perfecte et perpolitissime absolutae,.

la:verb:perpetuo.gloss: To cause to continue uninterruptedly, to proceed with continually, to make perpetual, perpetuate

la:adj:perpes.html:
perpes, ĕtis, adj.
like perpetuus, from per-peto
,
lasting throughout, continuous, uninterrupted, continual, perpetual (anteand post-class.): perpetem pro perpetuo dixerunt poëtae, Müll.: luna proprio suo perpeti candore, App. de Deo Socr. init.: silentium,: rivus cruore fluebat perpeti,.—
Esp., of time, continuous, never ending, perpetual, entire, whole: noctem perpetem,; ; : nocte perpeti,; : perpetem diem alternis pedibus insistunt,: per annum perpetem,: perpes aevi aeternitas, Mai.— Hence, adv.: perpĕtim, constantly, without intermission, perpetually, (but in , the correct read. is perpetuo; v. Sillig ad h. l., and Hand, Turs. 4, p. 465).

la:verb:perpetior.gloss: to endure (bear steadfastly), put up with, stand
senses: to endure (bear steadfastly), put up with, stand
to dare, venture, resist with courage and firmness
la:verb:perpetior.html:
per-pĕtĭor, pessus, 3,
v. dep. n. and a. [patior], to bear steadfastly, suffer with firmness or patience; to stand out, abide, endure (class.): animus aeger neque pati neque perpeti potis est, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 260 Vahl.): o multa dictu gravia, perpessu aspera, Cic. poët. Tusc. 2, 8, 20: facile omnes perpetior ac perfero,: mendicitatem,: dolorem,: affirmavi quidvis me potius perpessurum, quam, etc.,: casus illi perpetienti erat voluptarius,: mihi omnia potius perpetienda esse duco, quam, etc.,: dolorem asperum et difficilem perpessu,: audax omnia perpeti Gens humana, i. e. to dare, brave every consequence, ; : fulmina, noctem, imbres ... Perpetimur Danai,.—With object-clause: aliam tecum esse equidem facile possim perpeti,: neque me perpetiar probri Falso insimulatam,; ; : exscindine domos Perpetiar,: non tamen hanc sacro violari pondere pinum Perpetiar,.—With inf.: perpetiar memorare, i. e. will collect or control myself so as, etc., .—
Transf., of abstract things, to endure, put up with, etc.: vehementius quam gracilitas mea perpeti posset,.

la:noun:perpetuitas.html:
perpĕtŭĭtas, ātis, f.
perpetuus
,
uninterrupted or continual duration, uninterrupted progress or succession, continuity, perpetuity (good prose; cf. infinitas): non ex singulis vocibus philosophi spectandi sunt, sed ex perpetuitate atque constantiā,i. e. from their consistency,: ad perpetuitatem,to perpetuity, forever,: in vitae perpetuitate,through the whole course of our lives,: perpetuitas verborum,an unbroken succession,: sermonis,: dicendi,: laudis,.—In plur.: et opacae perpetuitates,unbroken tracts of land,. 1.

plecto
,

Lit.: figurae,; cf. ; : foramina linguae,: corpora terraï,: iter silvae,; : nervi,.—
Trop., intricate, involved, confused, perplexed, unintelligible, dark, ambiguous, obscure, inscrutable: sermones,: perplexius carmen,: perplexum Punico astu responsum,—As subst., intricacy, perplexity: ignorare se dixit, quidnam perplexi sua legatio haberet,.—Comp.: ratio perplexior,.—Hence, adv.: perplexē, confusedly, perplexedly, obscurely: pergin', scelesta, mecum perplexe loqui?: defectionem haud perplexe indicavere,; .—Comp.: perplexius errare,: disputans,.—
Carefully, with minute care: interrogando,.

la:verb:perpetro.html:
per-pĕtro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
patro
,
to carry through, complete, effect, bring about, achieve, execute, perform, accomplish; to commit, perpetrate (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.; rare as verb. finit.; syn.: perago, exsequor, conficio): perpetrat, peragit, perficit, Müll.: opus meum ut volui,: primā parte (operis) perpetratā, Müll.: perpetratā caede,; cf.: nemus, in quo perpetrata caedes erat,: id se facinus perpetraturos,: perpetrato sacro,: sacrificio rite perpetrato,; : pace nondum perpetratā,: perpetratis quae ad pacem deum pertinebant,: perpetrato bello,; : cujus (principis) jussu perpetratum ingenuitatis judicium erat,: ad reliqua Judaici belli perpetranda,; : quibus perpetratis,fin.; 15, 72 init.: perpetraret Anicetus promissa,fulfil,; ; : postremo quasi perpetraturus bellum, imperavit, etc.,: homicidium,: fraudem,: abominationem,: qui sibi manus intulit et non perpetravit,.—With ut or ne and subj., to bring it to pass that, that ... not, ; .—With inf.: male quod mulier facere incepit, nisi si ecficere perpetrat,.

senses: to drive, urge, force, enforce, constrain, compel
la:verb:perpello.html:
per-pello, pŭli, pulsum, 3, v. a.,
to strike or push violently.
Lit. (rare; perh. not in Cic., for in Cic. Cæl. 15, 36, the true reading is pepulerunt): nixurit, qui niti vult, et in conatu saepius aliquā re perpellitur, Nigid. ap. .—
Trop., to drive, urge, force, compel, constrain, prevail upon: perpulit, persuasit, impulit, Paul. ex Müll. (esp. freq. since the Aug. per.; in Curt. always with ut): si animus hominem perpulit, actum est; animo servibit, non sibi: sin ipse animum perpulit, dum vixit, victor victorum cluet,: ad deditionem,: callidum senem callidis dolis compuli et perpuli, ut. etc.,: numquam destitit Suadere, orare, usque adeo, donec perpulit,: Aulum spe pactionis perpulerat, ut, etc.,; : nec perpelli potuere ut, etc.,: perpellit, ut legatos ad Scipionem mittat,; : aliquem perpellere ne, etc.,.—With obj.-clause (so perh. only in Tac.): Mithridates Pharasmanem perpulit dolo et vi conatus suos juvare, (33); 11, 29; 13, 54.—
To impress deeply, make an impression on, influence: candor hujus te et proceritas, voltus oculique perpulerunt,.

la:adj:perperus.html:
perpĕrus, a, um, adj., = πέρπερος (prop. heedless, inconsiderate; hence, in gen.),
not properly constituted, faulty, defective, wrong (as adj. only ante- and postclass.): populares, Att. ap. : nihil perperum, (dub.; al. praeproperum).—Hence, adv.
perpĕram (adv. acc. fem. like clam, coram, palam; and in the plur. alias, alteras), wrongly, incorrectly, untruly, falsely (class.): loqui,: suadere aliquid,: insanire,: dicere aliquid, (Serv. ad loc.): si aspires perperam, Nigid. ap. : seu recte, seu perperam fecerunt,: recte an perperam judicare,: interpretari,; ; : pronunciare,.—
In a milder signif., erroneously, by mistake: ita dico, ne ad alias aedis perperam deveneris,; : perperam praeco non consulem, sed imperatorem pronunciavit,; Auct. B. Hisp. 12.—
perpĕrē, wrongly, falsely: opiniones perpere praesumptae,.

la:verb:perpendo.gloss: to weigh or examine carefully or exactly, ponder, consider
senses: to weigh or examine carefully or exactly, ponder, consider
la:verb:perpendo.html:
per-pendo, pendi, pensum, 3, v. a.,
to weigh carefully or exactly.
Lit. (very rare): in librili pendere,.—
Trop., to weigh carefully, examine; to ponder, consider (class.; syn.: delibero, expendo,

reputo): aliquid acri judicio,: diligentissime perpendens momenta officiorum,: aliquid ad disciplinae praecepta,: hoc non arte aliquā perpenditur,: judicare et perpendere, quantum quisque possit,: quid in amicitiā fieri oportet quae totā veritate perpenditur, which is considered or esteemed altogether according to its truth, : singulorum vires,: perpendendum erit praetori, cui potius subveniat,: ut ante perpensum et exploratum habeamus, an, etc.,: homo judicii perpensi,: deliberatio perpensa,.—Hence, per-pensē, adv., with deliberation, deliberately (post-class.); comp., ; .
